Functional Requirements Document · v1.0

Teknowgrade Learning Management System

A self-paced digital learning platform — course delivery, assessments, progress tracking, and certification, built for independent learners.

Client
Teknowgrade Pvt. Ltd.
Technology Partner
ALAR Innovations Pvt. Ltd.
Platform Type
Self-Paced LMS
Status
Draft for Review
01

Platform Objective

Teknowgrade requires a centralized Learning Management System that allows the institution to publish and manage educational and training content, while enabling students to independently access courses, consume learning material, take assessments, track their progress, and receive certificates upon successful completion.

Scope note The platform follows a self-paced learning model. There are no live classes or live teaching features in the initial scope — all training content (recorded videos, documents, presentations, assignments) is uploaded and managed by authorized teaching staff and admin users.
02

User Roles & Permissions

The platform is built around three primary user roles. Access narrows as it flows down the hierarchy — Administrators hold full platform control, Teaching Staff are scoped to their assigned courses and students, and Students interact only with their own learning journey.

Administrator

Full platform control, user & role management, course & enrollment oversight, system configuration, analytics & audit monitoring.

Teaching Staff

Create & manage assigned courses, upload content, build assessments, evaluate submissions, monitor progress. Scoped access only.

Student

Browse, enroll & learn at own pace. Watch videos, take notes, bookmark content, attempt assessments, earn certificates.

2.1 Student capabilities

Register / login
Complete profile
Browse available courses
Enroll in courses
Watch recorded lectures
Access course materials
Create personal notes
Bookmark / favorite content
Track course progress
Complete assignments
Take quizzes / exams
View scores / results
Retake eligible assessments
View & download certificates
View notifications
View learning history

2.2 Teaching Staff capabilities

Teaching staff are responsible primarily for content and academic management. Their access is restricted to courses, students, assessments, and data assigned to them — they do not have unrestricted administrative access.

Create / manage assigned courses
Upload recorded videos
Upload PDFs / documents / resources
Organize content into course → section → lesson
Create assignments, quizzes & examinations
Create question banks
Define marks & passing criteria
Review student submissions
Provide feedback
Monitor student progress

2.3 Administrator capabilities

User & role/permission management
Student & teaching staff management
Course & content management
Enrollment management
Assessment & certificate management
Dashboard / analytics & reports
System configuration
Notification management
Audit / activity monitoring
03

System Architecture

The platform is designed as a layered, service-oriented architecture. A responsive web client communicates through a single API gateway that enforces authentication and role-based access control (RBAC), routing requests to dedicated application services. Course content and video are separated from the core database and served through a controlled streaming/CDN layer, keeping media secure and the platform horizontally scalable.

Security note Rather than exposing downloadable video files directly, video is served through a controlled streaming layer so that direct public file access is minimized. The exact storage/streaming implementation is finalized during technical design.
04

Course Management & Content Structure

Course management is one of the core modules of the platform. Teaching staff and admins build courses using a consistent hierarchical structure — Course → Sections → Lessons — with an optional final assessment at the course level.

Each course can contain a mix of content and activity types:

Recorded videos
PDFs, PPTs & documents
External resources
Assignments
Quizzes
Exams
Projects
05

Video Learning Experience

Video is the primary content medium given there are no live classes. Students watch client-provided recorded videos directly through the LMS, with full playback controls and automatic, resumable progress tracking.

Recommended functionality

Video streaming with play / pause
Seek / rewind / fast-forward
Adjustable playback speed
Full-screen mode
Resume from last position
Watch-percentage tracking
Mark lesson as completed
Automatic course progress update

Example: a student watching Lesson 4 at 72% completion who leaves and returns later will resume approximately from where they stopped.

06

Personal Notes

A personal notes system differentiates the LMS from a basic video portal. Every student can create notes tied to the exact context in which they were written:

Note context Student + Course + Section + Lesson + Video Timestamp (optional)

Students can revisit all their notes for a course from My Courses → [Course] → My Notes.

Advanced option — timestamped notes

Students can attach a note to a specific video timestamp, e.g. "12:43 — Important concept about decorators." Clicking the note jumps directly to 12:43 of the video. This is recommended as a high-value differentiator for the platform.

07

Course Progress Tracking

Progress is tracked at multiple levels — lesson, section, and course — and rolled up into a single dashboard view for the student.

Lesson level: Completed / In Progress / Not Started
Section level: percentage completed
Course level: percentage completed
Calculated from lessons, video, assignments, quizzes, exams & required activities
08

Assessment Framework

8.1 Quiz Management

Teaching staff and admins can create quizzes without requiring development changes.

Quiz: Python Basics — 10 Questions · Maximum Marks: 20 · Passing Marks: 12 · Duration: 20 minutes

Supported question types: Multiple Choice, Multiple Correct Answers, True/False, Fill in the Blank. For the first release, the focus is on objective questions that can be automatically evaluated.

8.2 Examination Module

The LMS supports more formal examinations, configurable per course:

Exam name & course
Questions / question bank
Marks & passing percentage
Duration
Number of attempts
Random question selection
Random option ordering
Optional negative marking
Start / end availability window
Result visibility rules
Machine Learning Final Examination — 50 Questions · Duration: 60 min · Max Marks: 100 · Passing: 60% · Attempts: 2

8.3 Question Bank

A central question bank lets teaching staff create and categorize questions by course, section, topic, difficulty, question type, and marks. Exams can then automatically select questions from the bank, making the platform far more scalable.

Example rule: Select 20 questions · Topic: Python Functions · Difficulty: Medium · Marks: 2 each

10

Dashboards

10.1 Student Dashboard

The student dashboard is one of the primary screens, surfacing overall progress, active courses, upcoming activities, achievements, and recent activity at a glance.

10.2 Teaching Staff Dashboard

Teaching staff get an academic monitoring dashboard summarizing their courses, active students, average completion, pending evaluations, and upcoming exams — with drill-down from Course → Students → Individual Student.

10.3 Admin Dashboard

Admin gets the overall platform view, with KPIs and charts covering registrations, enrollments, course completion, assessment performance, certificates issued, and the most popular courses.

11

Certificate Management

Certificate management is a proper module rather than a simple PDF generator. When a student satisfies course completion requirements, the system automatically generates a certificate containing the student name, course name, completion date, certificate number, issuing organization, authorized signatory, a QR code, and a verification URL.

Certificate verification

A third party can scan the QR code to instantly verify authenticity:

Certificate ID: TG-2026-000123 · Student: [Name] · Course: Python Programming · Status: Valid

This adds significant credibility to the platform. Admin can additionally issue, revoke, reissue, download, search, and verify certificates.

Admin controls how students gain access to courses through three supported models:

Payment gateway integration is kept out of the initial MVP unless Teknowgrade specifically requires paid courses — this meaningfully reduces initial development complexity.
13

Notifications

An internal notification system keeps students and staff informed of key events:

New course assigned
New lesson available
Assignment deadline
Quiz available
Exam scheduled
Assessment result
Course completed
Certificate generated

Email notifications can be layered on top of this as part of the notification architecture.

14

Global Search

Students can search across courses, lessons, topics, and learning resources from a single global search bar — increasingly important as the content library grows.

15

Learning History

Each student maintains a complete learning history / learning profile containing:

Courses enrolled
Courses completed
Lessons watched
Assessments attempted
Scores
Assignments
Certificates
Notes
16

Gamification — Recommended Future Enhancement

Gamification is not mandatory for V1, but the platform should be architected so it can later support points, badges, achievements, course streaks, leaderboards, and learning milestones — e.g. "Python Beginner", "5 Courses Completed", "100% Course Completion". This can meaningfully improve student engagement in a later phase.

17

Mobile Responsiveness

Responsive web design is mandatory — students should be able to use the LMS from desktop, laptop, tablet, and mobile browsers. Native Android/iOS applications are not included in V1 unless specifically requested, and can be planned as a separate phase.

18

Recommended V1 Scope

The project is divided into three tiers to keep the initial release focused and de-risked, while leaving a clear path for growth.

Core MVP

  • Authentication & 3 user roles
  • Student profiles
  • Course / section / lesson management
  • Video streaming
  • Learning resources
  • Personal notes
  • Bookmarking
  • Progress tracking
  • Student / staff / admin dashboards
  • Assignments, quizzes & examinations
  • Question bank
  • Automatic & manual evaluation
  • Certificate generation & verification
  • Notifications
  • Reports
  • Responsive UI

Phase 2

  • Payment gateway
  • Advanced analytics
  • Gamification
  • Advanced question types
  • Advanced reporting
  • Email / SMS automation
  • Recommendation engine
  • AI-assisted learning features

Out of V1

  • Live classes
  • Video conferencing
  • Live chat teaching
  • Native mobile applications
  • Payroll / HRMS
  • CRM
  • Complex placement management
  • Marketplace functionality
